sanskrit_verse: द्रव्यमस्वामिविक्रीतं प्राप्य स्वामी समाप्नुयात् । प्रकाशं क्रयतः शुद्धिः क्रेतुः स्तेयं रहः क्रयात् ॥
transliteration: dravyam asvāmivikrītaṃ prāpya svāmī samāpnuyāt | prakāśaṃ krayataḥ śuddhiḥ kretuḥ steyaṃ rahaḥ krayāt ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Upon acquiring property sold without ownership by the seller, the true owner shall reclaim it. If purchased openly, the buyer is purified of wrongdoing; if bought secretly, the act constitutes theft.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority rests in rightful ownership, not transactional possession
Causation arises from knowledge and intent, not mere action
Capacity-based responsibility depends on visibility and inquiry capacity of the acquirer
Restoration logic mandates return to original lawful status
Consciousness alignment requires transparency and integrity in acquisition
executable_legal_axioms: IF property acquired AND seller lacks title THEN ownership remains with original proprietor
IF purchase made openly AND due diligence performed THEN buyer's claim is valid
IF purchase made secretly OR without verification THEN transfer invalidates acquirer's integrity
RETURN asset to original owner upon proof of unauthorized sale
RESTORE acquirer’s lawful standing through conscious acknowledgment and corrective action
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, courts must distinguish between good faith open-market transactions and concealed acquisitions. The threshold for responsibility lies in the acquirer's capacity for inquiry and alignment with dharma. Ownership rights supersede commercial exchange when title is defective.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Nyaya establishes that truth (ownership) cannot be displaced by false appearance (invalid sale). Responsibility flows from awareness and concealment. There is no punitive consequence—only realignment of property and consciousness back to their rightful order.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Reintegration of stolen property to its lawful owner
Completion process requiring the acquirer to acknowledge error and restore balance
Integrity restoration via public affirmation of corrected understanding
Responsibility assumption protocol wherein all parties align with factual ownership
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma prevails through restoration, not punishment. Ownership is consciousness-anchored. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness alone is the ultimate judge.
